content: CD226 is a glycoprotein with a molecular weight of approximately 65 kDa that is expressed on the surface of natural killer (NK) cells, platelets, monocytes, and a subset of T cells. It belongs to the immunoglobulin superfamily and contains two immunoglobulin-like domains of the V-set. CD226 plays a role in mediating cellular adhesion by binding to its ligands, CD112 and CD155, which are present on other cells. Additionally, cross-linking of CD226 with specific antibodies induces cellular activation.
